seal.hash_rule: sha256 over canonical JSON (sorted keys, no whitespace) of the predictions array
seal.note: Pre-registered 2026-11-14 00:58 UTC for 27 games (2026-11-14..2026-11-17) from the 2026-11-14 snapshot. Spread/total are model projections in half-point increments; no market price was available to this build, so no bet is asserted — only our number and the trigger level. These predictions must not be edited after tip-off: settle them with nba2.pipeline.settle. Verify the digest with `python -c "from nba2.models import ledger; print(ledger.verify(r'...'))"`.

calibration.title: Model parameters — derived, not assumed
calibration.blurb: These are the only two structural numbers the whole site depends on. Both are fitted against the verified standings snapshot; where the fit is weak we say so instead of quietly picking a convention.
calibration.source_note: Inputs: data/raw/team_ratings_2026-11-13.json (third-party). Win-loss verified three ways: NBA.com game cards (28/30 visible in that capture; TOR/WAS = FLAG-SLATE-02), the prior session's independent read (30/30), and a fresh upstream re-read on 2026-11-14 (30/30 identical — data/raw/ratings_recheck_2026-11-14.json).

values.method: least-squares fit of (sigma, hca) to the 30 verified win totals, grid 6.00-25.00 step 0.25 then refine step 0.01
values.sanity: NBA game margins are widely reported near 13-14 pts; our fit is independent of that

source.name: Derived: nba2.models.ratings
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Calibration + shrinkage computed from the verified snapshot at build time.

values.sanity: league home win rate implied by verified home/road splits = 51.1%; that rate alone implies a smaller h than the joint fit

source.name: Derived: nba2.models.ratings
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Calibration + shrinkage computed from the verified snapshot at build time.

values.method: unweighted mean of the 30 teams' PS/G

source.name: Derived: nba2.models.ratings
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Calibration + shrinkage computed from the verified snapshot at build time.

values.method: tau^2 = max(0, Var(SRS) - mean(se^2)), se = sigma/sqrt(games)
values.sanity: mean se = 3.99; shrinkage lambda therefore ~0.74-0.78 per team

source.name: Derived: nba2.models.ratings
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Calibration + shrinkage computed from the verified snapshot at build time.

values.method: model win total error at the optimum

source.name: Derived: nba2.models.ratings

source.note: Calibration + shrinkage computed from the verified snapshot at build time.

values.method: NOT fitted: no game-level totals available; used only inside the parlay sensitivity band
values.sanity: level-sensitive, so parlay output is reported as a ratio, not a price

The 2026-11-14 refresh re-checked all 31 games carried forward from the previous capture against a fresh retrieval — 0 field mismatches — and added the 11/17 games. The nine 11/13 games are day-before context (live or completed at retrieval time); they are priced for calibration and are never part of the sealed pick set.

picks.title: Picks — expressed as triggers, not as 'bets'
picks.blurb: A pick with no price is a guess. So each row states the number the market would have to show before our line justifies action, and the stake stays 0% until an odds feed exists. This is the honest shape of a line-origination desk before it has execution. The table covers the pick window from the snapshot's as-of date forward (today + 3 days max); the day-before context games are priced on the Lines page for calibration only.
picks.source_note: Triggers = our line ± 1.5 pts (unratified hurdle, see FLAG-LINE-03).

values.trigger: home spread ≥ +7.5 → take home; home spread ≤ +4.5 → take away
values.total_trigger: market total ≤ 233.0 → OVER; market total ≥ 236.0 → UNDER

injuries.title: Official NBA injury report — 11/13/26 19:30 ET release (freshest at build time; supersedes the 16:15 capture)
injuries.blurb: Transcribed from the NBA's own referee-operations PDF. The three middle columns are blank by policy: the report contains no minutes or production data, so any number we put there would be invented. P(plays) is our modelling convention for counting bodies, not a league probability. Covers 11/13 games plus the first official statuses for the 11/14 slate (five teams had still not submitted at this release).

A 'game flow analysis' that narrates those four columns without the data is storytelling, and it is how books get paid.

anomalies.title: Slate irregularities found while transcribing
anomalies.blurb: Recorded, not fixed. Each of these would corrupt an automated pipeline that trusted the pattern instead of the value.
anomalies.source_note: First recorded from https://www.nba.com/schedule retrieved 2026-11-13 22:39 UTC; dispositions updated where the 2026-11-14 capture resolves the question.

values.observation: Identical matchup and arena (Scotiabank Arena) as 0022600241 on 2026-11-15, two days apart. Both were read from the same official schedule page.
values.disposition: RESOLVED BY THE 2026-11-14 CAPTURE — the official page renders both games as distinct entries with distinct official game IDs, so this is a genuine schedule entry, not a duplicate card. Now inside the pick window; the rest/B2B consequences are priced by game flow and flagged.

parlays_xg.title: Cross-game parlays, and what stacking costs
parlays_xg.blurb: Two different games: the product rule is nearly right, so cross-game parlays are the safe place to express multiple views. Same game: the product rule is off by 13–26% on the ten quoted games above, which is larger than the entire edge a good model earns. And every leg you add multiplies the book's hold — arithmetic that needs no data to check.
parlays_xg.source_note: ρ = 0 assumed for cross-game (FLAG-CORR-05); -110 is a labelled placeholder price, not a quote.

gates.title: Validation gates — specification
gates.blurb: A strategy must clear all ten to be promoted and to receive rewards. Nine of the ten are currently blocked by missing data, which is the real status of this project and the reason the leaderboard is empty.

values.name: Sample size
values.rule: >= 300 settled bets for team markets; >= 500 for player props.
values.why: At -110 a 55% bettor needs roughly 300 bets before the standard error (sqrt(p(1-p)/n) ~ 2.9%) stops swamping a 5-point edge. Below this the leaderboard is ranking noise.
values.source: derived from the binomial standard error at p=0.55 — see research/05-skill-vs-luck.md
values.blocked: No settled bets yet. The ledger opened with the 2026-11-13 slate and was re-sealed for 2026-11-14..17.

source.name: Derived: nba2.models.lines
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Lines are arithmetic on the calibrated ratings; reproduce with `python -m nba2.pipeline.build_site_data`.

values.name: Closing line value (CLV)
values.rule: Mean CLV vs. closing number > 0 with a bootstrap 95% CI excluding 0.
values.why: CLV is the single least-luck-dependent measure of whether a line beats the market.
values.source: BLOCKED: requires a licensed odds feed (requirements R-101)
values.blocked: No market prices captured. Our lines are published, but nothing to beat them yet.

source.name: Derived: nba2.models.lines
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Lines are arithmetic on the calibrated ratings; reproduce with `python -m nba2.pipeline.build_site_data`.

values.name: Probability calibration
values.rule: Brier score <= 0.245 on settled games AND calibration slope in [0.85, 1.15] AND intercept in [-0.10, 0.10].
values.why: 0.25 is the Brier score of always forecasting 50%; a line-originator must beat that and be calibrated, otherwise the stake sizing is fiction.
values.source: derived: Brier (1950) definition; threshold is our own proposal (unratified)

source.name: Derived: nba2.models.lines
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Lines are arithmetic on the calibrated ratings; reproduce with `python -m nba2.pipeline.build_site_data`.

values.name: Line accuracy vs. naive baselines
values.rule: Mean absolute error of our spread must beat BOTH baselines: (a) 0.0 spread, (b) raw point-differential-per-game, by >= 0.30 points.
values.why: A line that only reproduces the standings' scoring margin adds no work; if shrinkage and schedule adjustment do not reduce error, delete the model.
values.source: derived from the snapshot baselines in nba2.models.gates
values.blocked: Needs settled games with official final scores.

source.name: Derived: nba2.models.lines
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Lines are arithmetic on the calibrated ratings; reproduce with `python -m nba2.pipeline.build_site_data`.

values.name: Luck removal
values.rule: Bootstrap (10,000 resamples, fixed seed) 95% CI of ROI excludes 0; t-stat >= 2.0; and the luck-adjusted PnL (each bet replaced by its model-expected PnL, variance kept) must not reverse the sign.
values.why: Separates 'won' from 'right'. A strategy whose PnL is explained by a few lucky bad beats fails here even if the record is positive.
values.source: derived: standard bootstrap / t-test; see research/05-skill-vs-luck.md

source.name: Derived: nba2.models.lines
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Lines are arithmetic on the calibrated ratings; reproduce with `python -m nba2.pipeline.build_site_data`.

values.name: Multiple-testing control
values.rule: Across every strategy ever evaluated in the same window, apply Holm-Bonferroni to the CLV t-tests and require the Deflated Sharpe Ratio > 0.
values.why: A leaderboard with N trials will produce a 'best' strategy by pure search. Punishing the number of tries is the only defence.
values.source: derived: Holm (1979); Deflated Sharpe = Bailey & Lopez de Prado (2014) formulation
values.blocked: Requires G-02 inputs and a complete trial ledger (see S-11).

source.name: Derived: nba2.models.lines
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Lines are arithmetic on the calibrated ratings; reproduce with `python -m nba2.pipeline.build_site_data`.

values.name: Walk-forward, no lookahead
values.rule: Every feature timestamped at or before tip-off; train on the first 70% of the window, test on the final 30%; test MAE must not exceed full-window MAE by more than 25%.
values.why: Ratings built from a standings snapshot include future games for the teams that played earlier; that leak is silent and fatal.
values.source: derived from our own ingest design (see research/01-line-origination.md 'point-in-time')
values.blocked: The current snapshot is a single as-of standings table, which is NOT point-in-time for games inside the week it covers. Backtests from this table would leak; only the forward ledger is clean.

source.name: Derived: nba2.models.lines
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Lines are arithmetic on the calibrated ratings; reproduce with `python -m nba2.pipeline.build_site_data`.

values.name: Parameter robustness
values.rule: Re-price the slate over the full sensitivity box of every unratified parameter; a pick is only published if its side is unchanged in >= 90% of the grid.
values.why: If a 10% change in sigma flips the pick, the pick is a parameter, not a signal.

source.name: Derived: nba2.models.lines
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Lines are arithmetic on the calibrated ratings; reproduce with `python -m nba2.pipeline.build_site_data`.

values.name: Cost and capacity
values.rule: Survive -110 vig, 1% hard-cap stake, 25% Kelly, and a re-quote of the model at the reference price minus 0.25 points of expected slippage.
values.why: Lines that only win before the vig, or before you move size, are not tradeable.

values.name: Availability-adjustment guardrail
values.rule: If a player on the official report with an Out/Doubtful status cannot be mapped to a quantified minutes delta, the line is published availability-blind and the game is marked INJURY-BLIND. No bet may be Tier A on an injury-blind game after the 13:00 ET report on game day.
values.why: Otherwise the model silently assumes injuries do not matter, which is exactly when a naive line is most wrong.

params.title: Every tunable number in the system, and whether anyone has justified it
params.blurb: This is the anti-overfitting page: any value whose status is not 'derived' or 'verified' is a place where a human could have cheated, so they are listed with their bands.

values.rationale: SD of a team's per-game margin. Searched over [6, 25]; the value used is the least-squares optimum against observed wins, so it is a fitted quantity, not an assumption.

values.rationale: Per-team James-Stein style reliability lambda = tau^2 / (tau^2 + se^2), where se = margin_sd / sqrt(games) and tau^2 = max(0, Var(rating) - mean(se^2)).

repo_review.blurb: Reviewed from the git history and the working tree, not from a summary of it.
repo_review.source_note: All findings also recorded in COORDINATION.md

values.finding: The repo began as a single 6-byte README.md containing '# NBA2'. There was no code, data, CI, licence or Pages configuration.
values.action: Nothing to inherit; everything below is net-new. Documented so no later session claims prior work existed.

source.name: This repository (git history)
source.class_label: Official NBA.com / NBA CDN
source.note: Repo review facts: commit list, file tree.

values.finding: No LICENSE file at any commit.
values.action: FLAGGED, not fixed: adding a licence is an owner decision, especially while third-party data is embedded (see Q-18).

source.name: This repository (git history)
source.class_label: Official NBA.com / NBA CDN
source.note: Repo review facts: commit list, file tree.

values.finding: Prior `data/injuries.json` published numeric impacts ('Starter out — ~0 min (vs. ~34 MPG season avg)', '-100% scoring/rebounding/playmaking output') that appear in no source. The official report has no minutes or MPG column.
values.evidence: `git show 821c175:data/injuries.json` keys: player, team, status, injury, game, minutesImpact, productionImpact, verified — no source field; report columns are Game Date, Game Time, Matchup, Team, Player, Status, Reason
values.action: Impact columns replaced with explicit blanks + FLAG-INJ-02. Rows kept and re-sourced to the official PDF.

source.name: This repository (git history)
source.class_label: Official NBA.com / NBA CDN
source.note: Repo review facts: commit list, file tree.

values.finding: Prior `data/strategies.json` attributed correlation coefficients (r ≈ 0.82, r ≈ 0.65) to https://www.nba.com/stats/help/faq, a help/FAQ page that contains no such values. The rows were labelled 'unverified' but still carried a source link that implies verification.
values.evidence: field `source` on those rows vs. the page's actual content
values.action: Removed. Correlations are now computed where possible (r(SRS, margin/G)) and blank elsewhere; a misattributed source is worse than no source.

source.name: This repository (git history)
source.class_label: Official NBA.com / NBA CDN
source.note: Repo review facts: commit list, file tree.

values.finding: Prior `data/picks.json` invented synthetic game IDs (GAME-20261113-001) for fixtures that have official IDs, and covered only 3 of the 9 games on 11/13.
values.action: Replaced with official IDs; slate now 31/31 games for the window.

source.name: This repository (git history)
source.class_label: Official NBA.com / NBA CDN
source.note: Repo review facts: commit list, file tree.

values.finding: Two GitHub Pages workflows deployed the same artifact: `.github/workflows/pages.yml` (cancel-in-progress: true) and `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` (cancel-in-progress: false), both `path: '.'`, both on push to main.
values.action: Consolidated to one workflow so a run cannot be cancelled mid-deploy by its twin (T-14).

source.name: This repository (git history)
source.class_label: Official NBA.com / NBA CDN
source.note: Repo review facts: commit list, file tree.

values.finding: The commit that added a working Pages workflow also states in README.md that the repository has 'no … automated deployment'.
values.evidence: `git show 821c175:README.md` contains 'no model' sentence; same commit adds deploy.yml
values.action: README rewritten to describe what exists and what does not.

source.name: This repository (git history)
source.class_label: Official NBA.com / NBA CDN
source.note: Repo review facts: commit list, file tree.

values.finding: Two parallel navigations existed: root `index.html` + `flagged.html` (session 1) and `pages/*.html` incl. `pages/flagged-review.html` (session 2), with different content on the same subject.
values.evidence: both files present in `main`; sidebar links to `pages/*` only
values.action: One nav, one Flagged page; root `flagged.html` converted to a redirect so old URLs do not rot.

source.name: This repository (git history)
source.class_label: Official NBA.com / NBA CDN
source.note: Repo review facts: commit list, file tree.

values.finding: Prior data files had no per-row source field, which is the specific thing the brief requires ('every table row must have a source link').
values.action: `make_row()` in nba2/provenance.py cannot produce a row without a source; lint re-checks the emitted JSON so the rule cannot be bypassed by editing site.json.

source.name: This repository (git history)
source.class_label: Official NBA.com / NBA CDN

values.finding: The prior injury page did cite real, correct official documents: Injury-Report_2026-11-13_01_00PM.pdf and _04_15PM.pdf exist at ak-static.cms.nba.com and their contents match what I independently retrieved.
values.evidence: both PDFs fetched; status/reason fields agree for the overlapping rows
values.action: Kept as the citation; only the invented numeric impacts were removed.

source.note: Repo review facts: commit list, file tree.

values.finding: No prior commit contained executable model code, so no published number could be reproduced by anyone.
values.action: Engine + deterministic rebuild (`python -m nba2.pipeline.build_site_data`) + reproducibility test.

values.finding: Prior COORDINATION.md recorded tasks as 'done' for pages whose tables were empty; the entries were honest about the emptiness but the status column overstated completion.
values.evidence: task table rows: 'No picks generated; lines blank' with status done
values.action: Board now distinguishes met / partial / blocked, and 'done' requires the artefact to work, not to exist.

values.finding: The prior 'correlation' values were presented without n, method or confidence interval, so they could not be challenged or reused.
values.action: Every correlation on this site now reports n and method, or is blank.

values.finding: Site publishes from the repository root, so every committed file (including data snapshots) is publicly fetchable — including any file a future session commits by accident.
values.action: Recommended only, not implemented: publish from a built directory (S-19). No secret is committed today (checked: no .env, no tokens in tree).

values.finding: The Nov 13 slate is entirely Emirates NBA Cup group play, while Nov 14-16 are ordinary regular-season games. Treating them as one distribution is an unexamined assumption in the prior design.
values.evidence: group labels on the official game cards (East/West Group A-C) vs blank groups for Nov 14+
values.action: Recorded as Q-06 with a Cup-group column on the slate page; model behaviour unchanged and disclosed.

source.name: This repository (git history)

source.note: Repo review facts: commit list, file tree.

values.finding: This sandbox has no outbound network except package/git hosts, so official data had to be brought in through the agent's fetch tools and committed as snapshots. That is a provenance property of the whole dataset, not a detail.
values.evidence: `curl https://www.nba.com` → 000; fetch tools return nba.com content
values.action: Snapshot files carry retrieved_at + URL + extraction notes; CI cannot re-fetch from here, hence R-104.

requirements.blurb: Every requirement in the brief, decomposed to something a reviewer can say yes/no to. Status is only 'met' when the artefact exists in the repository.
requirements.source_note: Decomposed from the project brief (Arena session request of 2026-11-13) plus the engineering requirements needed to satisfy it. Status is a self-assessment against files in this repository, reviewed by a human owner next.

questions.title: Open questions — the decision list
questions.blurb: Ordered by how much money a wrong answer costs, not by how interesting they are. Each row states what is already known so nobody re-asks it.
questions.source_note: Each row is a decision, not a curiosity: it says what we already have, what is missing, how to close it, and what changes in the model once it is answered. Anything I could resolve from an official source this session was resolved instead of asked.

values.question: Which odds source are we measuring against — and are we allowed to store its closing prices?
values.have: The full slate, our lines, and the knowledge that NBA.com renders odds client-side only and picks.nba.com publishes none.
values.missing: Any licensed book price, opening or closing, for any sport.
values.how: Owner picks a vendor (theScore Sportsdata/Odds API, Sportradar, or a sportsbook affiliate feed) and confirms storage rights; then add an ingest to data/raw.
values.impact: Everything. Without it there is no 'edge', no CLV, no gate G-02, no stake sizing, and no reason to prefer our number over a coin flip.

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.question: Is the product a line-setting desk or a betting-picks desk?
values.have: Both capabilities sketched: pricing engine (works) and bet selection with triggers (needs prices).
values.missing: Owner decision on primary objective.
values.how: Answer in one sentence; it changes which gate blocks promotion.
values.impact: A line-setting desk is graded on MAE/calibration and is buildable today with zero market data. A picks desk is not buildable until Q-01 is resolved.

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.question: What is the bankroll unit and the maximum stake per bet?
values.have: A config default of 1% hard cap and quarter-Kelly.
values.missing: Whether that is your risk tolerance at all.
values.how: Owner states units (e.g. 1 unit = 0.25% of bankroll).
values.impact: Kelly fraction, promotion criteria (G-09) and the reward pool's meaning.

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.question: Do we accept that game-day injury data arrives too late for a T-3 publication?
values.have: The official report's structure and cadence, plus proof: in the 11/13 16:15 ET release, all ten Nov 14 teams were 'NOT YET SUBMITTED'.
values.missing: Whether you want T-3 lines (injury-blind) only, or a T-0 re-issue after the 13:00 ET report.
values.how: Owner decision; implement as a second daily build at 13:30 ET.
values.impact: Determines whether '3 days in advance' is a feature or a self-inflicted handicap. Our lines currently apply no injury adjustment at all.

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.question: Can we get official player-level data (minutes, usage, on/off) from the build environment?
values.have: The knowledge that stats.nba.com endpoints are unreachable from here and nba.com/stats tables are client-rendered.
values.missing: An accessible official source or a licensed alternative.
values.how: Test from the CI runner (different network than this sandbox); if still blocked, evaluate a commercial feed.
values.impact: Props, prop combos, injury impact, and the margin/total correlation all sit behind this one answer.

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.question: Do Emirates NBA Cup group games belong in the same distribution as ordinary regular-season games?
values.have: The 11/13 slate is entirely Cup group play, and Cup games count for group standing with different incentives (winning by margin matters as a tiebreaker).
values.missing: Historical evidence on whether Cup games differ in pace, rotations or margin distribution.
values.how: Split the results snapshot by game_type once R-103 lands and test pace/margin differences.
values.impact: If Cup games differ, today's entire slate is mis-calibrated and the model needs a game-type effect or an exclusion rule.

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.question: Who ratifies the eleven unratified thresholds (disagreement tolerance, conviction cut, trigger hurdle, status→P(plays) weights, gate thresholds, ρ band)?
values.have: Every one of them written down with its rationale and band on the Parameters page.
values.missing: A decision, because they currently control which games are actionable.
values.how: Owner reviews the Parameters page and either accepts or edits config.py.
values.impact: Gate G-08 and Tier assignment are meaningless while thresholds are 'mine' rather than 'ours'.

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.question: Is a 12-game sample enough to trade at all?
values.have: Reliability weights ~0.74-0.78 and a fitted RMSE of 1.31 wins vs 2.78 baseline.
values.missing: Your risk policy for early-season modelling.
values.how: Owner decision; a hard rule could be 'no Tier A before 25 games'.
values.impact: Decides whether this slate should have produced zero picks rather than 31 lines.

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.question: What is the definition of 'removing luck' you will accept as a gate?
values.have: Four candidate mechanisms implemented: bootstrap CI on PnL, t-stat ≥ 2, calibration slope, and rewards weighted on CLV/accuracy rather than PnL.
values.missing: Whether you also require a variance-reduction metric (e.g. Sharpe of residualised PnL) or a holdout-only payout.
values.how: Owner picks; add to gates.
values.impact: Changes which strategies can win the leaderboard, and therefore what gets built next.

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.question: How do you want the leaderboard to treat strategies that bet different numbers of games?
values.have: Score components are per-bet averages, so abstention is neither rewarded nor punished beyond sample-size gates.
values.missing: Whether volume should carry weight (e.g. minimum coverage per slate).
values.how: Owner decision.
values.impact: A 'bet three games a season' strategy can look elite without a volume term.

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.question: Do we price parlays off our own singles only, or off book parlay prices when available?
values.have: Correlation-swept joint pricing on our own numbers; the ratio (not the level) is publishable today.
values.missing: Book parlay prices to compare against.
values.how: Comes free with Q-01.
values.impact: Determines whether S-04 is a strategy or an illustration.

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.question: What is the correct treatment of a two-way/G-League assignment listed on the injury report?
values.have: The report distinguishes 'G League - Two-Way', 'G League - On Assignment' and 'League Suspension' from injuries, and I count them as absent bodies.
values.missing: Whether those absences should affect a rotation-floor model identically to injury.
values.how: Owner decision; implement as a reason-class weighting in injuries.py.
values.impact: Our rotation index currently treats a suspended starter and a assigned two-way as similar 'missing bodies' at different weights.

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.question: Should rewards be paid at all before a strategy is promoted?
values.have: Allocation logic that pays nothing when nothing is promoted (pool 100% unallocated).
values.missing: Confirmation that you do not want an activity-based payout.
values.how: Owner decision.
values.impact: Paying for participation re-creates the exact incentive this project exists to remove.

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot

values.question: How should the site behave when the snapshot is stale?
values.have: as-of and generated-at stamps on every page, and the build refuses to run on a future-dated slate.
values.missing: A maximum-age policy (e.g. refuse to publish lines older than 24h).
values.how: Add to lint + a scheduled build.
values.impact: A 3-day-old line published as 'picks' is worse than no page.

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.question: What is the procedure when a game is postponed or a star is ruled out at warmups?
values.have: Nothing — the model has no re-quote path.
values.missing: Trigger for re-pricing and a rule for voiding sealed predictions.
values.how: Design a re-seal event in the ledger (new seal with reason, original kept).
values.impact: Settling against a cancelled game would corrupt the leaderboard.

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot

values.question: Which team is 'home' when the schedule says an arena hosts a neutral-site or international game?
values.have: None in this window; the schedule page marks neutralSite only in the JSON endpoints we cannot reach.
values.missing: A rule + a data field.
values.how: Add a `neutral` flag to the slate ingest, sourced from the game page.
values.impact: HCA would be wrongly applied and every line for that game shifts ~1.5-3 points.

values.missing: A licence/permission reading, or replacement with our own ingestion of official data.
values.how: Owner/legal reads the source's terms of use; or implement R-104 and delete the file.

suggestions.title: Site-improvement suggestions — review queue
suggestions.blurb: Nothing on this page has been implemented. Each item is written so a reviewer can accept, reject or defer it on its own merits, and the queue's state is the record of that decision.
suggestions.source_note: Nothing here has been implemented. Each item is written so it can be accepted, rejected or deferred on its own merits, and the Status column is the record of that decision — not of this session's opinion. Ordered by decision-quality gain per unit of effort.

values.title: Connect a licensed odds feed before anything else
values.problem: Without prices there is no edge, no CLV, no ROI and no way to know whether our line is good; the site can only publish projections and triggers.
values.proposal: Add `nba2/ingest/odds.py` writing dated snapshots to data/raw with book, market, line, price and timestamp; keep closing prices permanently.
values.benefit: Unblocks gates G-02, G-05 on real PnL, G-09, and converts every table from 'projection' to 'decision'.
values.risk: Vendor cost; storing closing lines needs storage rights (Q-18 style check).
values.recommendation: Accept first; nothing else on this list pays as well.

values.title: Ingest official game-level results daily
values.problem: σ, HCA, margin/total correlation, prop rates and every backtest all wait on game-level results; today they are fitted from a standings table instead.
values.proposal: Nightly snapshot of final scores by official game ID into data/raw; extend to ≥2 seasons for fitting.
values.benefit: Turns the two fitted constants into measured ones and kills the circularity in G-04.
values.risk: Needs network access from a runner (unavailable in this sandbox).
values.recommendation: Accept with S-01 in the same sprint.

values.title: Store point-in-time snapshots, not 'latest' tables
values.problem: An as-of standings table contains future information for games early in its window, which silently inflates any backtest (G-07 currently AT-RISK for exactly this).
values.proposal: Key every snapshot by (as_of_date, game_date) and make the model read only rows with as_of < tip-off.
values.benefit: Makes historical results believable at all; the single most common way a betting model dies.
values.risk: Storage growth; mitigation: parquet or compressed CSV in a data branch.
values.recommendation: Accept before any backtest is quoted on the site.

values.title: Ratify thresholds in one sitting
values.problem: Eleven numbers decide which games are actionable and who wins the leaderboard, and all eleven are currently mine.
values.proposal: Owner reviews the Parameters page and signs off (or edits) in a single commit; status flips from 'unratified' to 'ratified' in config.
values.benefit: Makes accountability real instead of implied; a one-hour task that removes a whole class of silent bias.
values.recommendation: Accept now — it blocks 'is this site trustworthy' more than any data purchase.

values.title: Preregister strategy trials with a counter
values.problem: G-06 (multiple-testing control) is unpayable while nobody records how many variants were tried; the Deflated Sharpe needs N.
values.proposal: Append every evaluation attempt (id, config hash, timestamp, seed) to data/trials.jsonl; leaderboard reads N from it.
values.benefit: Makes the leaderboard a science instead of a search result; costs ~20 lines.
values.risk: Requires discipline to log failed attempts too — that is the point.
values.recommendation: Accept; pair with a rule 'no evaluation without registration'.

values.title: Render 'why is this blank' on every empty cell
values.problem: A blank cell reads as 'no data' but not as 'which missing input, and what would fill it'.
values.proposal: The generator already attaches flag ids to blanks (see the strict rule in nba2/provenance.py::make_row): render the flag id as a tooltip on each blank cell, linking to its entry on the Flagged page.
values.benefit: Turns every gap into a one-click work item for the reviewer instead of a mystery.
values.risk: Adds ~40 lines of build logic; must stay in sync with the flag registry.
values.recommendation: Accept — cheap and it is what the Flagged page exists for.

values.title: Staleness banner with an explicit expiry
values.problem: Lines published from a 3-day-old snapshot look identical to fresh ones; nothing on the page says 'stop'.
values.proposal: Header banner computing age of snapshot vs a policy max age (e.g. 24h), turning red past expiry and disabling the picks tab.
values.benefit: Prevents the most expensive realistic failure: betting yesterday's number today.
values.risk: Needs the scheduled rebuild (S-16) to be meaningful.
values.recommendation: Accept with S-16.

values.title: Replace third-party ratings with an official snapshot
values.problem: Every line currently derives from Basketball-Reference values (PS/G, PA/G, SRS) because the official endpoint was unreachable here; that is flagged (FLAG-RAT-01) but it is the load-bearing wall.
values.proposal: When R-104 is possible, ingest official team stats at a fixed daily time and delete the third-party file; keep both during a parallel period to measure drift.
values.benefit: Removes the largest single caveat on the site and satisfies the 'official source' rule literally.
values.risk: Official endpoint access/licensing (see Q-18's twin problem).
values.recommendation: Accept after S-02.

values.title: Structured injury-PDF parser instead of text extraction
values.problem: 17 of 91 rows needed team attribution from block continuation because the PDF table breaks across pages (FLAG-INJ-01).
values.proposal: Parse the report with a table-aware reader keyed on the Game Date column, and store page/row coordinates for each record.
values.benefit: Kills the attribution caveat and lets the site assert completeness ('all 7 pages parsed').
values.risk: PDF layout changes without notice mid-season.
values.recommendation: Accept; it is a correctness fix, not polish.

source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot

values.title: Add a game-day re-issue build (T-0) alongside the T-3 build
values.problem: Injury reports for future days are 'NOT YET SUBMITTED' — proven this session — so a 3-day-ahead line is structurally injury-blind.
values.proposal: Publish two sealed snapshots per day (T-3 and T-0 after the 13:00 ET report) and show the delta between them as the injury signal.
values.benefit: Converts a weakness into a measurable quantity: how much our line moves on availability news, which is a strategy family of its own.
values.recommendation: Accept — the best idea on this list for model quality per unit of data.

values.title: Show per-line contribution of every input
values.problem: 'San Antonio -4.5' is opaque: nobody can see how much is rating gap, shrinkage, HCA or injury-blindness.
values.proposal: Add a decomposition column (SRS gap ×λ, raw-margin gap ×λ, HCA, injury adj) per line, computed not asserted.
values.benefit: Reviewers can disagree with a component instead of the whole number; that is how a model gets better.
values.recommendation: Accept.

values.title: Bankroll/staking page with the actual policy applied
values.problem: Stakes are pinned to 0% by rule until prices exist, which is correct but explains nothing to a reviewer.
values.proposal: A page showing the staking maths with the current caps and what a bet would look like at each available price once S-01 lands.
values.benefit: Makes the 0% legible as a policy rather than a gap.
values.risk: Must not become a calculator that implies a recommendation.
values.recommendation: Accept with a disclaimer requirement.

values.title: Per-game chart: rating gap vs line, with the disagreement band
values.problem: Tables answer 'what number' but not 'how near the decision boundary is this game'.
values.proposal: Small multiples drawn client-side from site.json; the band is the sensitivity box, so a narrow bar = fragile line.
values.benefit: Fragile picks become visible without reading the stability column.
values.risk: Chart code must render the same numbers as the table or we get two truths; generate from the same JSON.
values.recommendation: Defer until S-01/S-02 so there is something worth drawing.

values.title: Table ergonomics: sticky headers, density toggle, CSV export
values.problem: The 31-row lines table and 91-row injury table are the working surface; today they scroll freely and cannot be exported.
values.proposal: Sticky thead, a compact-density class, and a per-table 'download CSV' that includes the source column.
values.benefit: Reviewers can work offline without losing provenance — export keeps the source link per row.
values.recommendation: Accept.

values.title: Accessibility and print path
values.problem: A dense analytical dashboard with no ARIA table semantics and no print stylesheet is hard to review with colleagues.
values.proposal: scope=headers, caption elements, focus styles, and a print stylesheet that keeps source URLs.
values.benefit: Reviewable in a meeting, which is where decisions actually happen.
values.recommendation: Accept.

values.title: Scheduled rebuild with a freshness gate
values.problem: The site updates only when a session commits; the numbers are a frozen 2026-11-13 snapshot.
values.proposal: Daily Actions workflow that re-ingests, rebuilds, re-seals, and fails (not publishes) if any official source is unreachable.
values.benefit: Ends the 'is this current?' question. Failure to fetch becomes visible instead of silent staleness.
values.risk: Runner needs network to the official endpoints; a failing schedule must not publish a stale site.
values.recommendation: Accept once S-02 exists.

values.title: Compliance framing on the front page
values.problem: A public page that prints spreads, parlays and staking language reads as betting advice; today the notice is a footer line.
values.proposal: Front-page notice: research tool, no guarantees, 21+/jurisdiction responsibility, links to problem-gambling help.
values.benefit: Reduces real-world harm and the risk of the site being read as a tipster service.
values.recommendation: Accept.

values.title: Keep the sealed ledger in git, not a database
values.problem: A leaderboard is only credible if predictions cannot be edited after the fact.
values.proposal: Keep the current design: canonical JSON + sha256, committed with the site build; never rewrite history.
values.benefit: Auditable by anyone with the repo, with no infrastructure to trust.
values.risk: Git history bloat over a season; mitigate with monthly squash archives.
values.recommendation: Already applied; keep unless a DB is required for scale.

values.title: Publish from a build directory instead of the repository root
values.problem: `path: '.'` makes every committed file public, including data snapshots and anything a future session commits by mistake.
values.proposal: Build to `site/` (HTML + assets + data/site.json) and publish that directory only.
values.benefit: Reduces accidental disclosure; keeps the public surface explicit.
values.effort: M (changes every relative link + breaks current live URLs unless redirected)
values.risk: URL churn; needs a redirect plan for the already-live root pages.
values.recommendation: Defer — real improvement, but it breaks existing links and none of the currently committed files are sensitive.

values.title: Stop writing narrative into empty analysis columns
values.problem: The temptation this site is built to resist: a 'game flow' page with adjectives where pace numbers should be.
values.proposal: Keep policy as code (blank + flag is the only permitted empty state) and add a lint rule that fails any prose-only analysis column.
values.benefit: The property that makes everything else on the site usable as evidence.
values.recommendation: Already applied via make_row + lint; do not weaken it under time pressure.

The durable fix is structural — own a directory and a data namespace, as `originated/**` did — not a stricter merge rule.

x3way.title: Three originated lines for the same games — and how much of the gap is convention
x3way.blurb: Mean |gap| across 31 games: 2.9 pts as published, 2.7 pts once session 3's own injury adjustment is stripped out using the fields it published. The reduction is the point: two teams reading the same official data and disagreeing by 6 points are usually disagreeing about a *parameter*, and a parameter nobody ratified is not evidence.

xadjudicate.blurb: Two sessions disagreed on six statuses and both believed they had read the same document correctly. A third session had ingested the 17:15 ET revision, which is later than ours, so the disagreement is now testable instead of a matter of trust. This is what 'verify against official sources' is actually worth: not a claim of care, but a second and third copy to compare against.

flags.title: Flagged for review — every unverified value on this site
flags.blurb: This page is the deliverable. If a number is not here and not blank, it was confirmed against an official source; if you find otherwise, that is a bug.

values.statement: The official schedule lists POR @ MIN on 2026-11-16 AND 2026-11-17 (0022600250, 0022600254, both Target Center), and NYK @ TOR on 2026-11-15 AND 2026-11-17 (0022600241, 0022600253, both Scotiabank Arena). The 2026-11-14 capture renders both pairs as distinct official game entries with distinct game IDs, resolving the earlier 'duplicate card?' question: these are genuine schedule entries. Unusual, but real.
values.action: Game flow already prices the POR@MIN pair as a same-venue back-to-back; no model change needed. Keep monitoring for postponements.
